newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota town recovers from flooding.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota town recovers from flooding.

text.p: Icy floodwaters from the overflowing Knife River receded on Monday and residents who had evacuated over the weekend began returning to their mud-splattered homes.
"We had about 200 people displaced, and a lot of them still have water in their homes," Beulah Mayor Darold Benz said. "A lot of people are sick and sore, but we were lucky that nobody got hurt."

He described several rescues late on Saturday and early Sunday in the town of 4,500 people, including one couple's narrow escape when their pickup truck stalled in an icy stream. "They were up to their necks in ice water when they got rescued," Benz said.

Several elderly people had to be saved when they tried to wait out the flooding but became trapped in waters that inundated the basements and first floors of some 150 homes in the south end of Beulah.
Weather forecasters warned of further flooding along creeks and rivers across the region as the winter's record snowfall melted.

Ice-jams along the Knife and Cannonball Rivers poured floodwaters into small towns where residents and volunteers stacked sandbags, set up pumps and dug channels through the snowbanks to guide runoff away from vulnerable homes.
Another storm dumped three inches (eight cm) of snow on Bismarck, the state capitol 50 miles (80 km) southeast of Beulah.
National Weather Service hydrologist Charlene Prindiville said she expected to issue flood warnings to residents living near Apple Creek, a few miles (km) east of Bismarck.
"There are still problems with flooded roads and farmland," Prindiville said. Many of the areas in danger of flooding were sparsely populated, she added.

The storm dumped a layer of heavy, wet snow on the eastern half of the state where some of the worst spring flooding was anticipated in the coming weeks. Dozens of towns along the Red River on the state's eastern border were hurriedly erecting earthen levees to divert the expected floodwaters.
